subject: We want a service credit
body: Your API was down for three hours last Tuesday. We expect a service credit on this month's invoice.

draft.reply: Hello, and we're sorry about the disruption you experienced last Tuesday. Service credits are defined in the Enterprise SLA. If monthly uptime falls below 99.9%, the account owner can request a credit under Billing > SLA claims within 30 days of the incident. Please have your account owner submit the claim there soon so it falls within that window. Please note that support agents can't grant or promise credits, so we can't confirm that a credit will be applied to this month's invoice. The claim is reviewed through that process. You can also follow incident updates on our status page at status.helpline.example.

subject: Refund our annual plan
body: We bought the annual plan five days ago and it doesn't fit. Please refund it.

draft.reply: Thanks for reaching out, and sorry the plan isn't the right fit. Annual plans can be refunded pro rata within 14 days of purchase or renewal, and since you purchased five days ago you are within that window. Refund decisions are made by our billing team rather than by support, so we are opening a billing request on your behalf and they will follow up with you directly. I can't confirm the refund or its amount myself. If you'd rather change plans than cancel, upgrades take effect immediately and downgrades take effect at the end of the current billing period.

subject: Discount or we leave
body: A competitor is 30% cheaper. Match it or we cancel at renewal.

draft.reply: Thanks for letting us know, and for considering staying with Helpline. I'm not able to offer or approve discounts or price matching from support, so I'm passing your ticket to a team member who can review your request and discuss options ahead of your renewal. If it helps, please share your renewal date and the competitor's plan details you're comparing against.

subject: Waive the extra seats
body: We were billed for 7 seats we never used. Please take them off this invoice.

draft.reply: Thanks for reaching out. I can't remove charges from an invoice myself, because billing adjustments are decided by the billing team. I can help with the seat count, though. Billing counts every user who isn't deactivated, including invited users who haven't accepted yet. If some of those 7 seats are pending invitations, you can remove them under Admin > Users, which lowers your seat count going forward. If the seats were charged on an annual plan purchase or renewal within the last 14 days, a pro rata refund may be possible. I'm passing your request to our billing team so they can review this invoice and follow up with you.

subject: Logins from an unknown country
body: Our admin account shows successful logins from a country none of us has been to. What do we do?

draft.reply: Thanks for flagging this. Successful logins from a location none of your team has visited could mean the account is compromised, so please treat it as a security concern. This ticket is being passed to our security team, who review every report within 1 business day. In the meantime, please don't paste passwords or full tokens into this ticket. If you share details, include only the approximate login times and the country shown so the team can investigate.

subject: Lost phone with authenticator
body: One of our admins lost the phone with the authenticator app. Can they still get a code by SMS?

draft.reply: Yes, in most cases. According to our documentation, SMS remains available as a fallback for two-factor sign-in unless an admin has disabled it. If SMS hasn't been disabled for your workspace, the admin can choose SMS to receive a code and sign in. Once they are back in, they can set up the authenticator app again on their new phone under Profile > Security by choosing Authenticator app and scanning the new QR code.
